submission.justification: Crystal-K3 has the best resolution (about 2.9% FWHM at 5 cm), but its intrinsic background is 2.0 ± 0.2 counts/kg/day. That is 4 times the hard limit of 0.5, and the background comes from contamination inside the crystal itself, so shielding cannot fix it. K3 is therefore ruled out. Of the two crystals within the background limit, K2 (0.30 counts/kg/day) has much better resolution than K1 (0.10 counts/kg/day, about 8.6% FWHM at 5 cm). Scanning K2 thickness gave these resolutions: 2 cm 5.11%, 3 cm 4.84%, 4 cm 4.39%, 4.5 cm 4.33%, 5 cm 4.42%, 5.5 cm 4.51%, 6 cm 4.51%, 8 cm 4.97%, 10 cm 6.63%. The best value is at about 4.5 cm. The curve is flat between 4 and 5 cm, and the differences there may be within simulation statistics, so any thickness from 4 to 5 cm performs about the same. Trade-off: we give up about 1.4 percentage points of resolution compared with K3 in order to meet the hard background requirement.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 662 keV
requirements.evidence: K2 at 4.5 cm gives 4.33% FWHM, the best simulated value among crystals that meet the background limit. K3 is better (2.9%) but fails the background limit.

requirements.requirement: Crystal must be one of the three candidates

requirements.evidence: Assay result for K2: 0.30 ± 0.05 counts/kg/day (Q1 2026 campaign, query_assay).

requirements.requirement: Submit one recommended crystal and thickness
